extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, patent attorneys and agents practicing before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct that govern practitioner behavior when practicing before the USPTO, including their relationship to the ABA Model Rules and the regulatory citation (37 CFR Part 11). Also describes OED assistance available to practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (replacement and conformity)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (USPTO Rules) replaced the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and conform to the Model Rules of Professional Conduct of the American Bar Association, versions of which have been adopted by 49 states and the District of Columbia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO Rules are the controlling professional conduct standards for practitioners before the USPTO; they were adopted to bring USPTO professional responsibility obligations into alignment with the ABA Model Rules. Practitioners should treat the USPTO Rules as the governing code for conduct when practicing before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with state bar requirements / streamlined obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Rules streamline practitioners' professional responsibility obligations, thereby aligning those obligations with most practitioners' state bar requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should recognize that the USPTO Rules were designed to reduce conflicts and differences between USPTO obligations and state bar rules. When evaluating compliance, consider both USPTO Rules and applicable state bar rules; the USPTO Rules aim to be consistent with the rules adopted by most states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory citation: 37 CFR Part 11
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR Part 11 contains the regulatory language implementing the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct. Practitioners should consult Part 11 for the precise regulatory provisions, obligations, and enforceable standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED assistance (scope and limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED also offers practitioners assistance with issues relating to registration and practice before the USPTO. While OED cannot provide you with legal advice or render an opinion on your compliance with the rules, we can provide callers, who may remain anonymous, with information regarding which professional conduct rules should be considered in a given situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on OED as a source of legal advice or formal compliance opinion. Use OED as a resource to identify relevant professional conduct rules and for administrative assistance related to registration and practice. For legal advice about compliance, seek counsel; for rule identification or administrative questions, contact OED (phone number provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult Final Rule and comparison materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Links provided to the Final Rule (Federal Register notice), Proposed vs. Final USPTO Rule Comparison Chart, ABA and USPTO Rule Comparison Chart, USPTO Press Release, USPTO Director's Blog, Proposed Rule and Comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should review the Final Rule, comparison charts, and related materials to understand differences between prior and current rules, rationale for changes, and how the USPTO Rules map to ABA Model Rules and state rules. These materials can clarify interpretation and transitional issues.
